Subject: Unexplained token surge on 2026-09-17 — request for adjustment

Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well. Our finance team flagged a 3.1x spike in billed tokens on 2026-09-17 compared to our 7-day average (see attached CSV). We didn’t change traffic patterns and our app reported a series of 504s around 09:22–09:28 PDT followed by automatic client retries. We suspect the retries were charged in full.

Can you confirm whether these retries were deduplicated by Redwood? If not, we need a billing adjustment or credit for tokens that were duplicate retries. Per our contract we expect retries to be handled idempotently where possible.

Attached: usage_export_20260917.csv (summary from our side).

Best,
Samantha Chen

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexplained token surge on 2026-09-17 — need root cause and adjustment

Quick summary from infra: we saw a transient upstream 504 from one of our regional frontends at 09:22:31 PDT. A subset of clients retried and our current ingestion path did not honor an idempotency key for generation requests by default — client retries were treated as separate requests.

Evidence: request logs show ~2.9x duplicate groups for the affected tenant in the 09:22–09:27 window; payload hash and token counts match across duplicates. There is no sign of partial truncation or truncation-caused double counting — these are full duplicate generations.

Impact: estimated 1.8M tokens double-billed for Commercio on 2026-09-17 (preliminary). We also found a misclassification in the billing aggregator where deduplication flags were not applied when frontend returned 504s instead of 5xx.

Action plan:
- We will issue a proactive billing credit equal to the duplicated token quantity (1.8M tokens) plus a $0.00 rounding policy (Marissa, confirm value).
- Engineering will deploy a short-term patch within 6 hours to treat generation requests with identical payload hashes in a 10s window as duplicates for hosted API traffic.
- We will prepare a formal incident note and include the delta export for Commercio.

Attaching: billing_adjustment_20260918.pdf (draft credit memo).

-Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha@commercio.ai>
Cc: Commercio Billing <billing@commercio.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Resolution & credit for duplicated tokens on 2026-09-17

Hi Samantha — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Short summary and next steps below.

What happened:
- On 2026-09-17 at ~09:22 PDT one regional frontend returned intermittent 504s. Several of Commercio’s clients retried requests. Due to a gap in our ingest deduplication logic, the retries were treated as independent generations and were billed.

What we did:
- We estimated 1,805,240 duplicated tokens for your account for 2026-09-17 (attached CSV excerpt).
- We’re issuing a billing credit for that exact token quantity; the draft credit memo is attached (billing_adjustment_20260918.pdf). Your September invoice will reflect the adjustment within 3 business days.
- Engineering implemented a short-term patch to deduplicate identical payloads in a 10s window for hosted endpoints; a more robust idempotency control is in our roadmap.

Attachments: billing_adjustment_20260918.pdf, usage_export_20260917.csv (annotated), ingest-log-snippet.txt

Ask: please confirm you’re comfortable with the credit and whether you’d like the adjustment to appear as a token credit or as a monetary reduction on the September invoice. Also tell us if you want the full incident note and technical postmortem sent to your security/ops team.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we’ll refund the duplicated tokens and follow up with a formal incident report.

Best,
Mina
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
